scores.claim_text: SAIC generated approximately $7.4 billion FY2022 revenue with 98% from U.S. government contracts.

M_value.top_award_desc: Systems and Computer Resources Support for U.S. Army RDECOM Software Engineering Directorate

scores.interpretation: USAspending confirms multi-billion-dollar DoD obligation base consistent with $7.4B FY22 revenue and 98% U.S.-gov mix. Top award is a major Army RDECOM IDIQ. No divergence — concentration claim is substantiated.

scores.claim_text: U.S. Army 15% / U.S. Navy 12% / Other DoD 21% of FY2022 revenue.
scores.interpretation: J-Book corpus (410 PEs from FY26 books, contractor-indexed) returns no contractor-name hits for SAIC under either short or full name. This is expected: SAIC is primarily an O&M / services integrator, not a hardware prime, and most of its work flows through IDIQ task orders that do not surface as named contractors in R-2 / P-40 exhibits. Coverage gap, not a red flag — see calibration heuristic #7.

scores.claim_text: Approximately 1,900 active contracts and task orders.
scores.interpretation: Even the top 25 awards confirmed via usaspending sum to ~$10.8B, consistent with the disclosed diffuse 1,900-contract portfolio. Diffusion itself reduces program-specific J-Book exposure (good for survivability, bad for thesis identifiability).

scores.claim_text: Majority of forward business expected via IDIQ / GSA Schedule / multi-award competitive bidding.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_dod_contracts; consistency with disclosed 1,900 task orders
scores.interpretation: USAspending top awards visibly follow IDIQ task-order ID patterns (W31P4Q05A0031 = Army RDECOM IDIQ vehicle). Forward-pipeline narrative is consistent with the actual contracting structure. No PE-level divergence to score.

scores.claim_text: USMC AAV program terminated for convenience October 3, 2018; SAIC still negotiating cost recovery as of Jan 28, 2022.
scores.interpretation: The AAV program is a USMC ground combat vehicle line that pre-dates our FY26 J-Book corpus snapshot — it would have appeared in earlier USMC P-40 procurement exhibits. The termination is SELF-DISCLOSED by SAIC (no divergence to catch); the only residual risk is the cost-recovery dispute, which is a P&L tail, not a J-Book signal. Treat as UNVERIFIABLE via J-Book; the underlying fact is admitted in the filing.

scores.claim_text: Forward opportunity narrative: 'broadband, cyber, climate resiliency' from infrastructure bill.
scores.interpretation: Nine cyber-related Air Force / OSD PEs match the keyword but fall outside the 2023-01-15 cutoff window in our corpus, so no funded/unfunded status can be assigned. More importantly, the company never names any of these PEs in the filing — the 'cyber/broadband/climate resiliency' language is generic marketing, not a J-Book-grounded forward claim. Cannot score divergence on hand-waving.

scores.claim_text: Rollup acquisition cadence: Unisys Federal (2020, ~$1.0B financed), Koverse (2021), Halfaker (2021, $100M financed).
scores.M_check: acq_coherence.score_acquisition_coherence(parent_thesis='pure-play government IT services / digital transformation', acquisitions=[Unisys Federal, Koverse, Halfaker])
scores.interpretation: Acq-coherence subagent flags INCOHERENT_ROLLUP, but with low-confidence reasoning (cited insufficient data on each target). The Unisys Federal deal IS revenue-synthetic in the strict sense (purchased existing federal-IT book of business). Soften to MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY rather than RED — the rollup signal is real but the subagent did not have rich target-side data. Watch-item, not a kill-shot.

scores.claim_text: $2.54B long-term debt; $2.1B variable-rate debt; $518M FY22 op cash flow.
scores.interpretation: No external EDGAR full-text hits flagging covenant trouble. Coverage ratio (op CF $518M vs $148M FY23 LTD maturities + $77M interest) is comfortable. Leverage is real but service-able. No divergence.

scores.claim_text: ~4M sq ft, 160 offices, 31 states; Reston VA HQ.
scores.M_check: epa_frs.query_facility (not in catalog for this run)
scores.interpretation: EPA FRS source is not registered in this catalog instance; SAIC's footprint is office space (not regulated manufacturing facilities) so EPA FRS would not be informative anyway. Control claim — accepted at face value.

scores.claim_text: Sensitive IC agencies named as customers, but no specific IC program or PE disclosed.
scores.interpretation: Counterparty disclosure on IC work is intentionally vague (as expected for clearance-required programs). No external EDGAR cross-references found. Correctly UNVERIFIABLE — and this is the SIGNAL: an entire business line is asserted with zero verifiable hook.

summary.key_finding: SAIC discloses ZERO named Pentagon Program Elements and ZERO named forward programs of record. Revenue is reported only by service branch (Army 15% / Navy 12% / Other DoD 21% / Other federal 50%) and spread across ~1,900 task orders. The J-Book Exposure Divergence pattern requires a company to name specific programs the framework can falsify; SAIC's filing is structurally immune to this pattern because it discloses no falsifiable program-specific forward claims. The only real signal is acq_coherence flagging the FY20-FY22 rollup (Unisys Federal + Koverse + Halfaker) as low-mean-coherence — but that is an orthogonal signal, not a J-Book divergence. Framework correctly returns 'mostly UNVERIFIABLE' here, which is the right answer for diffuse IT-integrator filings.
summary.framework_calibration_note: This filing tests the FALSE-POSITIVE rate of the J-Book module. The module did not generate any false SEVERE/RED signals on a filing that names no PE numbers. That is the desired behavior. The cohort gains a true-negative observation: SAIC is the control case for the J-Book Exposure Divergence pattern.
